title: Conveyor
statementMd:
Anton came to a chocolate factory. There he found a working conveyor and decided to run on it from the beginning to the end.

The conveyor is a looped belt with a total length of $2*l*$ meters, of which $*l*$ meters are located on the surface and are arranged in a straight line. The part of the belt which turns at any moment (the part which emerges from under the floor to the surface and returns from the surface under the floor) is assumed to be negligibly short.

The belt is moving uniformly at speed $*v*_{1}$ meters per second. Anton will be moving on it in the same direction at the constant speed of $*v*_{2}$ meters per second, so his speed relatively to the floor will be $*v*_{1} + *v*_{2}$ meters per second. Anton will neither stop nor change the speed or the direction of movement.

Here and there there are chocolates stuck to the belt ($*n*$ chocolates). They move together with the belt, and do not come off it. Anton is keen on the chocolates, but he is more keen to move forward. So he will pick up all the chocolates he will pass by, but nothing more. If a chocolate is at the beginning of the belt at the moment when Anton starts running, he will take it, and if a chocolate is at the end of the belt at the moment when Anton comes off the belt, he will leave it.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7fcbe21ac233256be6e14c9e08608208248d66ce.png) The figure shows an example with two chocolates. One is located in the position $*a*_{1} = *l* - *d*$, and is now on the top half of the belt, the second one is in the position $*a*_{2} = 2*l* - *d*$, and is now on the bottom half of the belt.

You are given the positions of the chocolates relative to the initial start position of the belt $0 ≤ *a*_{1} < *a*_{2} < ... < *a*_{*n*} < 2*l*$. The positions on the belt from $0$ to $*l*$ correspond to the top, and from $*l*$ to $2*l*$ — to the the bottom half of the belt (see example). All coordinates are given in meters.

Anton begins to run along the belt at a random moment of time. This means that all possible positions of the belt at the moment he starts running are equiprobable. For each $*i*$ from $0$ to $*n*$ calculate the probability that Anton will pick up exactly $*i*$ chocolates.

## Input

The first line contains space-separated integers $*n*$, $*l*$, $*v*_{1}$ and $*v*_{2}$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$, $1 ≤ *l*, *v*_{1}, *v*_{2} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the number of the chocolates, the length of the conveyor's visible part, the conveyor's speed and Anton's speed.

The second line contains a sequence of space-separated integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($0 ≤ *a*_{1} < *a*_{2} < ... < *a*_{*n*} < 2*l*$) — the coordinates of the chocolates.

## Output

Print $*n* + 1$ numbers (one per line): the probabilities that Anton picks up exactly $*i*$ chocolates, for each $*i*$ from $0$ (the first line) to $*n*$ (the last line). The answer will be considered correct if each number will have absolute or relative error of at most than $10^{ - 9}$.

## Note

In the first sample test Anton can pick up a chocolate if by the moment he starts running its coordinate is less than 0.5; but if by the moment the boy starts running the chocolate's coordinate is greater than or equal to 0.5, then Anton won't be able to pick it up. As all positions of the belt are equiprobable, the probability of picking up the chocolate equals ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/55d1d7955c1e59f407eb6baa7601582a54eeac4f.png), and the probability of not picking it up equals ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0e79ad74cc0314b318cc094369c845c55b37c9ef.png).
statementZhMd:
安东来到了一个巧克力工厂。在那里，他发现了一条正在工作的输送带，于是决定从起点跑到终点。

输送带是一条环形传送带，总长度为 $2*l*$ 米，其中有 $*l*$ 米位于地面上，并且呈直线排列。传送带在任意时刻发生转弯的部分（即从地板下方露出到地面、以及从地面返回地板下方的部分）均认为长度可以忽略不计。

传送带以每秒 $*v*_{1}$ 米的速度匀速运动。安东将沿传送带运动的方向，以每秒 $*v*_{2}$ 米的恒定速度在传送带上奔跑，因此他相对于地面的速度为每秒 $*v*_{1} + *v*_{2}$ 米。安东既不会停下，也不会改变运动速度或方向。

传送带上到处粘着一些巧克力（共 $*n*$ 块）。它们随传送带一起运动，并且不会从传送带上掉落。安东喜欢巧克力，但他更希望向前跑。因此，他会拿起所有自己经过的巧克力，但不会拿其他巧克力。如果安东开始奔跑时某块巧克力正位于传送带起点，他会拿起它；如果安东离开传送带时某块巧克力正位于传送带终点，他将不会拿起它。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7fcbe21ac233256be6e14c9e08608208248d66ce.png) 图中展示了一个有两块巧克力的例子。其中一块位于位置 $*a*_{1} = *l* - *d*$，当前在传送带的上半部分；另一块位于位置 $*a*_{2} = 2*l* - *d*$，当前在传送带的下半部分。

给出巧克力相对于传送带初始起点的位置 $0 ≤ *a*_{1} < *a*_{2} < ... < *a*_{*n*} < 2*l*$。传送带上从 $0$ 到 $*l*$ 的位置对应上半部分，从 $*l*$ 到 $2*l*$ 的位置对应下半部分（见样例）。所有坐标均以米为单位。

安东在一个随机时刻开始沿传送带奔跑。这意味着，他开始奔跑时传送带的所有可能位置等概率出现。对于每个 $*i*$（从 $0$ 到 $*n*$），计算安东恰好拿起 $*i*$ 块巧克力的概率。

## 输入格式

第一行包含四个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$、$*l*$、$*v*_{1}$ 和 $*v*_{2}$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$，$1 ≤ *l*$、$*v*_{1}$、$*v*_{2} ≤ 10^{9}$）——巧克力的数量、传送带可见部分的长度、传送带的速度以及安东的速度。

第二行包含一组用空格分隔的整数 $*a*_{1}， *a*_{2}， ..., *a*_{*n*$（$0 ≤ *a*_{1} < *a*_{2} < ... < *a*_{*n*} < 2*l*$）——巧克力的坐标。

## 输出格式

输出 $*n* + 1$ 个数，每行一个：对于每个从 $0$（第一行）到 $*n*$（最后一行）的 $*i*$，输出安东恰好拿起 $*i*$ 块巧克力的概率。如果每个数的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 9}$，则答案被认为是正确的。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，如果安东开始奔跑时巧克力的坐标小于 0.5，他就可以拿起这块巧克力；但如果男孩开始奔跑时巧克力的坐标大于或等于 0.5，那么他将无法拿起它。由于传送带的所有位置等概率，拿起这块巧克力的概率等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/55d1d7955c1e59f407eb6baa7601582a54eeac4f.png)，而不拿起它的概率等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0e79ad74cc0314b318cc094369c845c55b37c9ef.png)。
